purpose: The loader architecture as a hierarchy (filesystem -> archive -> compression -> subsystem parser -> owner), not a flat list of loader functions.

layers.name: container format
layers.description: BIGF/BIG4 directory format (Task 5, unmodified). Confirmed to cover every .big and .viv file sampled across the corpus (355 files by magic byte).

layers.name: compression
layers.description: Two distinct compression layers confirmed in this corpus: RefPack (10 FB/90 FB, Task 5) for the vast majority of archive members, and a newly-proven zlib-based '.zlb' format (4-byte declared size + standard zlib deflate) for 26 loose files (boot-load screens and paired venue/environment assets under enviro/). Both are decode-proven with self-consistent round trips.

layers.name: resource dispatch (two distinct mechanisms found)

mechanisms.example: func_001AD694 (0x001AD694) -- opens preload/db.viv once, tests a 10-bit caller-supplied bitmask, and requests the named xdbNNNN.adf member per set bit.
mechanisms.per_table_loader: func_001A0C74 (shared, reused verbatim by all 10 xdb tables)

mechanisms.description: A 9-entry, 16-byte-stride array found at ELF virtual 0x567D60 (file offset 0x567E60 in the raw ELF), each entry {name_ptr: char*, word1: u32 (0x100 for 8/9 entries, 0x500 for one), word2: u32 (1 for 8/9 entries, 4 for one), word3: u32, a small category id 0x10-0x23}. Lists (in order): misc.viv (referenced but not present anywhere in the currently-tracked corpus -- a genuine gap, not assumed away), boxersh.viv, actors.viv, cboxshr.viv, boxerpre.viv, allhair.viv, boxmisc.viv, boxmisc2.viv, tables.viv.
mechanisms.discovery_method: This table was found by raw-byte search, not by the automated string/xref extraction pass -- see 'methodology_note' below.
mechanisms.consuming_function: Not located in this pass: no code xref to the table's own base address (0x567D60) was found by either the automated reference extractor or a manual raw-pointer search; one further indirection (a pointer to the table stored at ELF virtual 0x6DE908) was found in a data region, but the function that dereferences that pointer was not located. This is recorded as STATIC_PENDING, not assumed.

layers.methodology_note: The automated string/xref extraction pass missed all 4 of boxersh.viv/cboxshr.viv/boxmisc.viv/boxmisc2.viv's string references (0 hits) even though a direct raw-byte search of BOOT.BIN found each exactly once, at the exact file offset the pre-existing (pre-evidence-standard) audit in _audit_output/ had separately noted. This was independently re-verified in this pass, not taken on the audit's authority. The practical conclusion: absence from the automated string/reference extraction is not proof a resource is unreferenced -- a raw-byte search is required before concluding no reference exists.

layers.name: XDB schema classification and row access
layers.description: func_001AD268 iterates header.word0 field descriptors, not boxer records: it scans the packed 2-bit-per-field type table at payload+0x18 and builds caller-shaped classification output (callers use strides 1, 5, and 0x28). The generic row path is now separately mapped: func_001AD21C returns header.word1 as record_count; func_001AD180 bounds record_index against word1 and selects the row-major token matrix using stride word0*2; func_001ACCAC bounds field_id against word0; func_001ACD40 resolves type 0/1/2/3 as inline int16/string/int32/float32.
layers.significance: This corrects the former per-record interpretation of word0 and the +0x18 bitmap. In xdbboxr.adf, word0=121 fields, word1=37 records, the type bitmap is 31 bytes, and the row matrix begins at +0x38 with 0xF2-byte records.

layers.name: object ownership / UI consumption
layers.description: func_001AF768 is the fight-session singleton constructor, not a UI/menu constructor. It embeds XDB classification helpers near +0x19F4/+0x1A08, calls func_001AD268 with strides 5 and 0x28, and then initializes further subsystems. A separate SelectBoxer AIP path is now mapped through GetSelectBoxerInfo/UpdateSelectBoxerInfo; UpdateSelectBoxerInfo reaches concrete boxer rows/fields through the generic XDB accessors.
layers.unresolved: Meaning of the stride-5/stride-0x28 classification outputs and the remaining fight-session init chain; semantic field IDs outside the recovered SelectBoxer rating block.
